correctness.rationale: With t coins all excesses 0,…,2t over t(pk+1) are attainable, so passage to multiples of p gives the stated represented intervals J_t. They are empty up to t_p−1, nonempty thereafter, with both endpoints strictly increasing. Thus the interval before J_{t_p} has exactly kt_p missing integers and, between J_t and J_{t+1}, the number of missing integers is the positive part of k−2q−floor(3r/p), with t=pq+r. Within each quotient block this is nonincreasing, with unchanged value at wraparound because p≥3. At q=0 the j=0 residue class is excluded precisely by t≥t_p; all classes occur at q≥1. For 1≤ℓ<k the odd deficit k−ℓ picks the middle class only; the even deficit ≥2 picks the outer pair, including the valid last class at q=0 when k−ℓ=2. This gives the histogram and the unique length kt_p. Counting the two deficit parities and then weighting by ℓ gives the stated block count and genus. This covers p=3 and k=2 without appeal to the finite diagnostic; the worked example (7,8) has 24 blocks and genus 116.
residual_risks: The proof and review concern the stated quotient family, not an arbitrary three-coin progression or a representation-count p-gap statistic.

evidence: The prior gap decomposition holds for every a≥3, so a=pk+1 is within scope even at k=2.

evidence: Substituting a=pk+1 into the prior endpoints gives the projected interval [kt+ceil((3t+1)/p), k(t+1)+floor(t/p)]. Its nonnegative length is the prior summand k+floor(t/p)−floor(3t/p).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: For 0≤t<ceil(p/3) the intervals are [kt+1,k(t+1)] and merge into the initial run. From t≥ceil(p/3) onward, the complementary represented interval [kt+ceil(t/p),kt+floor(3t/p)] is nonempty and separates consecutive positive projected gaps. Setting t=pq+r now gives length k−2q−floor(3r/p): the residue classes of floor(3r/p) equal to 0,1,2 have sizes t_p,c_p,p−t_p−c_p. Odd deficits select class 1 and positive even deficits select classes 0 and 2. This is direct specialization and residue counting from a prior exact theorem, including the endpoint merge and k=2; it does not depend on recovering information from the scalar genus.

value.rationale: The histogram is a natural and useful refinement of genus in principle. In this submission the exact histogram and apparent transition at p=4 follow by elementary residue counting and merging the initial projected intervals from an existing complete gap description. No independently useful exact fact beyond that mechanical extraction survives the value requirement for a narrow invariant.
